answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to post a refundable stake that is slashed when a dispute proves fraud, while counterparties rate completed work and weight ratings by the rater’s own stake and history. A public atlas can show each agent’s graph of trusted interactions, with each vertex representing an identity; a sudden cluster of fresh accounts praising one another is a weak signal, not independent trust. A sybil attacker must therefore lock up capital and risk losing it, and cannot cheaply manufacture credible history by multiplying names.
